THE PROBLEM A filter can match content. It cannot read context. 1 No notice to the publisher. Rule 4(4) requires a notice only to users trying to view the content. Rule 4(8), for a platform’s own removals, requires notice, reasons and a chance to dispute. 2 Human review is optional in practice. The rule mentions “appropriate human oversight” but attaches 3 No order to see. LiveLaw says it was never shown the request or direction behind any restriction. 4 Slow appeals. 7 days for the grievance officer, 30 to appeal, then an “endeavour” to decide in 30 more. News is stale by then. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 05 / 08

WHAT LIVELAW ASKS FOR The reliefs sought 1 Strike down the “exactly identical” requirement, or read it down to exclude news and court reporting, with prior notice and human review. 2 Quash two unpublished MeitY advisories of 8 and 10 October 2026, one addressed to Meta alone. 3 Make MeitY, the Home Ministry and Meta produce every “legal request” behind the restrictions. 4 No restriction of LiveLaw’s account without a court order, a Rule 3(1)(d) intimation or a Section 69A direction given to LiveLaw. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 06 / 08

WHERE IT STANDS Notice issued; hearing in January 19 Nov 2026 Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma issues notice to the Union and Meta; four weeks to reply. Interim relief was not pressed. The Centre’s offer The ASG suggested treating the petition as a representation and passing a reasoned order. LiveLaw’s counsel called that “a mere formality”. 18 Jan 2027 Next hearing. Similar challenges are listed on 9 February 2027. The big question: Shreya Singhal upheld blocking under Section 69A because it came with reasons and a hearing. Can a mandatory filter skip both? Adv. Ashwani Kumar 07 / 08

MY TAKE Filters for abuse material, yes. Filters for news need a human and a reason. Automated matching makes sense for child sexual abuse material. Applied to journalism and court reporting, it decides what citizens can know without telling anyone why. Should a machine ever restrict a news report before a person has looked at it? Adv.
